question: Ross (1992) Table 2 (decision ross1992-tables, reverted by the user): how are its PAn phonemes and its phonetic symbols entered?
chosen_reading: As rows of source ross1992 on eight lects (Proto-Atayal, Saisiyat, Thao, Proto-Bunun, Proto-Amis-Sakizaya for Ross's Amis, Proto-Rukai, Proto-Puyuma, Proto-Paiwan). *Z, *d1, *d2, *d3 are entered as *z, *d, *Z, *D of the Ross system (Ross 2015), following the equivalences already in the notes of the Ross notation rows; Blust (2013: 577-578) traces *d1-*d3 to Dahl (1976) and *Z to Dyen (1951) and rejects both. The other phonemes are those of the default system (*L = *N; *s and *S undivided). Ross's phonetic symbols are respelled in IPA (č t͡ʃ, ¢ t͡s, š ʃ, ṭ ʈ, ḍ ɖ, ṛ ɽ, ḷ ɭ, lʸ ʎ, ř ɾ, r̃ r, ḳ q, γ ɣ, y j; the belted l with a ring ɬ and without one ɮ) with his symbol in source_form; 'x-y-z' is initial, medial, final; a slash is two rows with conditions unknown; bracketed allophones are in the notes. The values are Ross's readings of the sources of 1956-1988 and differ in places from the rows of the newer sources (Proto-Bunun *q > k; Proto-Paiwan *b, *w as a bilabial fricative). Where the lect's inventory already has a symbol for the same phoneme the reflex is respelled to it (the table RESPELL in the script: Proto-Atayal t, γ, č, š, ɬ as t̪, ɡ, t͡s, s, l; Saisiyat ṛ, l, z̪, u, s̪ as ʐ, ɾ, ð, o, θ; Thao n, ɬ, r̃ as n̪, ɬ̪, ɾ̪; Proto-Bunun d, b, c as ʔd, ʔb, t͡s; Amis ʔ, ɬ, v, h as ʡ, ɮ, b, ħ; Proto-Rukai and Proto-Puyuma t, d as t̪, d̪, Proto-Puyuma l, ṛ as l̪, ɭ; Proto-Paiwan β as v), with Ross's symbol in source_form.
alternatives: 1. A separate system 'Ross 1992' on PAn with *d1, *d2, *d3, *Z, *L, *ʔ as its symbols. 2. Enter the Proto-Tsou column (s1/s2, s3; Ross's own Proto-Tsouic, 'a little' different from Tsuchida's): there is no Proto-Tsou or Proto-Tsouic lect, and Ross (2012) argues against Tsouic. 3. Enter PAn *ʔ (kept in Proto-Bunun and Amis): the PAn inventory here has no *ʔ. 4. Enter the PMP column and Table 3 (PAn, PMP, Tagalog, Javanese, Toba Batak, Malay, POc; p. 28): PAn > PMP and PMP > POc are rows from newer sources, and Tagalog and Javanese are not lects. 5. Respell the reflexes to the symbols of each lect's newer rows that are still Ross's (Proto-Atayal d, Amis r, Proto-Puyuma ʔ, Proto-Paiwan z, Proto-Bunun k for *q).
